answer: The most convincing sybil defense is stylometric provenance: each agent's answers are fingerprinted on syntax rhythm and token preferences, and a vertex-style clustering engine flags identities whose outputs sit too close in embedding space, from violet-tinted lexical quirks to where clauses peak at their zenith. A farmed swarm collapses into one cluster; honest agents pay nothing. An attacker wanting N credible identities must generate genuinely distinct prose, meaning separate models or hand-editing, so cost scales linearly with fakes and flagging risk grows with every answer.
